judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

N. Anand Venkatesh, J.:— The petitioner is the wife of the detenu viz. Jain Melord, S/o. Yesudhasan, aged 46 years. The detenu has been detained by the second respondent by his order in P.D. No. 28/2025, dated 8-9-2025 holding him to be a “Sexual Offender”, as contemplated under Section 2(ggg) of the Tamil Nadu Act 14 of 1982. The said order is under challenge in this Habeas Corpus Petition.

2. We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and the learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondents. We have also perused the records produced by the detaining authority.

3. Though several grounds have been raised in the Habeas Corpus Petition, the main ground that was urged by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner is that it was a solitary case against the detenu and according to the detenu, a false case has been foisted against him and the trial is also pending before the concerned Special Court dealing with POCSO offences and the victim girl has already tendered evidence and has been cross examined.

4. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor, on instructions, submitted that considering the gravity of the offence, even if it is a solitary case, a detention order can always be passed and the law on this issue is well settled. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor confirmed the fact that the victim girl has been examined on the side of the prosecution and she has also been cross examined on the side of the detenu.

5. In our considered view, the detenu is facing trial in the ground case and it is a solitary case without any previous antecedents against the detenu. That apart, the victim girl had already been cross examined before the trial court. Hence, the prevailing penal law can sufficiently take care of this situation and it does not require a detention order to be passed against the detenu.

6. We are clarifying that such an observation is made considering the facts of the present case and this cannot be taken as a precedent in cases where detention orders are passed based on a solitary offence.

7. In the result, the Habeas Corpus Petition is allowed and the order of detention in P.D. No. 28/2025, dated 8-9-2025 passed by the second respondent is set aside. The detenu viz. Jain Melord, S/o. Yesudhasan, aged 46 years, is directed to be released forthwith unless his detention is required in connection with any other case.
